newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pulls back from highs on origin offer.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pulls back from highs on origin offer.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures stepped back from early sharp rise on aggressive origin selling into the advance but the market finished Thursday midsession higher.
By the midday break, nearby months were still about $40 up after scooping some $60-$70 gain early in the session.
Traders said the gains were sustained by commission houses who return back to cover their short positions after selling at the opening.
Benchmark July stood $42 up at $1,660 a tonne by the end of the morning trade after a session high of $1,690, just $10 short of its key resistance.
The contract had gapped $52 up at the open against pre-market expectations of $100 higher.

May, which enters the month-long tender period on Thursday, was thinly-traded and still up $38 at $1,576. Uncovered positions fell further to 2,347 lots by Wednesday's close from 3,815 a day before as the first tender day neared.
By the midday pause, LIFFE said 791 five-tonne lots were tendered. There were no re-tenders.
At the height of the coffee rally in March, a total of 15,890 tonnes were delivered against the March contract, the largest quantity tendered since March 1993.
There was earlier talk that a large European trade house seeking to tender a large quantity of Thai coffee against May contract.
Overall volume reached 2,726 lots, dominated by the July contract.
New York coffee powered higher on Wednesday on speculative buying amid continued concerns over nearby availability.
"...There is little sign of where coffee will come from to satiate demand over the nex few months," broker GNI said.

The rally since 1997 had triggered heavy front-loading of origin shipments especially from Central and South America, and this could leave a supply void until their next main harvest at the end of this year.
